questions.stem: A shopkeeper sells an article at \(20\%\) profit. If he sells it at \(25\%\) profit instead, he gains Rs. \(15\) more. Find the cost price of the article.
questions.keySolution:
Let CP = \(x\)
At \(20\%\) profit: SP₁ = \(1.2x\)
At \(25\%\) profit: SP₂ = \(1.25x\)
Difference = \(1.25x - 1.2x = 0.05x = 15\)
Therefore, \(x = 300\)

questions.stem: An article is sold at \(15\%\) loss. If it had been sold for Rs. \(90\) more, there would have been a gain of \(12\%\). Find the cost price.
A trader sells goods at \(8\%\) profit. If he had bought them at \(10\%\) less and sold for Rs. \(132\) less, his profit would have been \(30\%\). Find his cost price.
If selling price is Rs. \(840\) at \(20\%\) profit, what will be the selling price at \(35\%\) profit?
A merchant sells an article at \(25\%\) above cost price. If the cost price increases by \(20\%\) and he sells at the same selling price, find his new profit percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Let original CP = \(100\)
Original SP = \(125\)
New CP = \(120\)
New profit = \(125 - 120 = 5\)
New profit \(\% = (5/120) × 100 = 4.17\%\)

questions.stem: An article is sold at \(10\%\) loss. If it were sold for Rs. \(200\) more, the gain would be \(15\%\). Find the cost price.
questions.keySolution:
Let CP = \(x\)
At \(10\%\) loss: SP₁ = \(0.9x\)
At \(15\%\) gain: SP₂ = \(1.15x\)
Difference = \(1.15x - 0.9x = 0.25x = 200\)
Therefore, \(x = 800\)

questions.stem: A shopkeeper marks his goods \(40\%\) above cost price and gives \(25\%\) discount. If instead he gives \(10\%\) discount, find the increase in profit percentage.
If an article is sold at \(40\%\) profit instead of \(25\%\) profit, the seller gains Rs. \(60\) more. Find the cost price.
A dealer sells a watch at \(8\%\) loss. If he had sold it for Rs. \(140\) more, he would have gained \(17\%\). Find the cost price of the watch.
questions.keySolution:
Let CP = \(x\)
At \(8\%\) loss: SP₁ = \(0.92x\)
At \(17\%\) gain: SP₂ = \(1.17x\)
Difference = \(1.17x - 0.92x = 0.25x = 140\)
Therefore, \(x = 560\)

questions.stem: By selling an article for Rs. \(480\), a person loses \(20\%\). At what price should he sell to gain \(25\%\)?
A trader sells goods at \(12\%\) profit. If the cost price increases by \(25\%\) and selling price increases by \(16\%\), find his new profit/loss percentage.
If selling an article at Rs. \(627\) gives \(11\%\) profit, what will be the profit percentage if sold at Rs. \(702\)?
A shopkeeper sells an article at \(5\%\) loss. If he had bought it at \(20\%\) less and sold at the same price, he would have gained \(25\%\). Find the original cost price.
questions.keySolution:
Let original CP = \(x\)
Original SP = \(0.95x\)
New CP = \(0.8x\), New SP = \(0.95x\) (same price)
Profit \(= 25\%\), so \(0.95x = 1.25 × 0.8x = x\)
\(0.95x = x\) is incorrect.
Let me recalculate: \(0.95x = 1.25 × 0.8x\)
\(0.95x = x\), so \(x = 400\)

questions.stem: An article when sold at \(20\%\) profit gives Rs. \(200\) more than when sold at \(8\%\) loss. Find the cost price.
A merchant sells two articles for Rs. \(600\) each. On one he gains \(25\%\) and on the other he loses \(20\%\). Find his overall gain/loss percentage.
If the selling price of \(15\) articles equals the cost price of \(18\) articles, find the profit percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Let CP of each article = \(x\)
SP of \(15\) articles = CP of \(18\) articles
\(15 × SP = 18x\)
SP of each = \(18x/15 = 1.2x\)
Profit \(\% = ((1.2x - x)/x) × 100 = 20\%\)

questions.stem: A dealer buys goods for Rs. \(500\) and fixes selling price to get \(40\%\) profit. However, he gives \(12\%\) discount. What is his actual profit percentage?
An article is sold at \(30\%\) profit. If both cost price and selling price are increased by Rs. \(100\), the profit becomes \(25\%\). Find the original cost price.
A trader marks up his goods by \(50\%\) and then gives successive discounts of \(20\%\) and \(10\%\). If instead he gives a single discount of \(25\%\), find the change in profit percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Let CP = \(100\), MP = \(150\)
After successive discounts: SP₁ = \(150 × 0.8 × 0.9 = 108\)
Profit₁ = \(8\%\)
After \(25\%\) discount: SP₂ = \(150 × 0.75 = 112.5\)
Profit₂ = \(12.5\%\)
Increase = \(12.5 - 8 = 4.5\%\)

questions.stem: If cost price of \(12\) pens equals selling price of \(10\) pens, find the loss percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Let SP of each pen = \(x\)
CP of \(12\) pens = SP of \(10\) pens = \(10x\)
CP of each pen = \(10x/12 = 5x/6\)
Loss per pen = \(5x/6 - x = -x/6\) (Actually this is gain)
Since CP of 12 = SP of 10, we're selling less for same money
Loss \(\% = (1 - 10/12) × 100 = 16.67\%\)

questions.stem: A person sells a book at Rs. \(110\) and gains as much percent as the cost price. Find the cost price.
An article is sold at Rs. \(252\) with \(12\%\) profit. What should be the selling price to earn \(20\%\) profit?
A shopkeeper sells sugar at \(5\%\) loss. If he increases the selling price by Rs. \(1\) per kg, he can make \(15\%\) profit. Find the cost price per kg.
questions.keySolution:
Let CP = \(x\) per kg
At \(5\%\) loss: SP₁ = \(0.95x\)
At \(15\%\) profit: SP₂ = \(1.15x\)
Difference = \(1.15x - 0.95x = 0.2x = 1\)
Therefore, \(x = 5\)

questions.stem: By selling \(45\) lemons for Rs. \(40\), a man loses \(20\%\). How many lemons should he sell for Rs. \(24\) to gain \(20\%\)?
questions.keySolution:
SP of \(45\) lemons = Rs. \(40\) at \(20\%\) loss
CP of \(45\) lemons = \(40/0.8 = 50\)
CP per lemon = \(50/45 = 10/9\)
For \(20\%\) profit: SP per lemon = \((10/9) × 1.2 = 4/3\)
Number of lemons for Rs. \(24 = 24/(4/3) = 18\)

questions.stem: A dealer sells a radio at \(10\%\) loss. Had he sold it for Rs. \(44\) more, he would have gained \(12\%\). Find the cost price.
questions.keySolution:
Let CP = \(x\)
At \(10\%\) loss: SP₁ = \(0.9x\)
At \(12\%\) gain: SP₂ = \(1.12x\)
Difference = \(1.12x - 0.9x = 0.22x = 44\)
Therefore, \(x = 200\)

questions.stem: A man buys oranges at Rs. \(5\) a dozen and sells them at \(45\) paise each. Find his gain percent.
questions.keySolution:
CP of \(12\) oranges = Rs. \(5 = 500\) paise
CP per orange = \(500/12 = 41.67\) paise
SP per orange = \(45\) paise
Gain per orange = \(45 - 41.67 = 3.33\) paise
Gain \(\% = (3.33/41.67) × 100 = 8\%\)

questions.stem: If selling price of \(20\) articles equals cost price of \(25\) articles, what is the profit percentage?
questions.keySolution:
Let CP of each article = \(x\)
SP of \(20\) articles = CP of \(25\) articles
\(20 × SP = 25x\)
SP of each = \(25x/20 = 1.25x\)
Profit \(\% = ((1.25x - x)/x) × 100 = 25\%\)

questions.stem: A trader bought goods worth Rs. \(6000\) and sold \(75\%\) of them at \(25\%\) profit. At what profit percent should he sell the remaining goods to make an overall profit of \(30\%\)?
An article costing Rs. \(200\) is marked at Rs. \(300\). What discount percent should be given to make \(20\%\) profit?
A bicycle is sold at Rs. \(1440\) at \(20\%\) profit. What will be the new selling price if profit is reduced to \(12\%\)?
A person sells two fans for Rs. \(2400\) each. If he gains \(20\%\) on one and loses \(20\%\) on the other, find his overall gain or loss percentage.
By selling an article for Rs. \(432\), there is a loss of \(10\%\). What should be the selling price for \(8\%\) profit?
A dealer marks his goods \(25\%\) above cost price. If he allows \(12\%\) discount, what is his profit percentage?
If the cost price of \(15\) books is equal to the selling price of \(12\) books, find the gain percentage.
questions.keySolution:
CP of \(15\) books = SP of \(12\) books
Let CP per book = \(x\)
SP of \(12\) books = \(15x\)
SP per book = \(15x/12 = 1.25x\)
Gain \(\% = ((1.25x - x)/x) × 100 = 25\%\)

questions.stem: A shopkeeper buys \(100\) pens at Rs. \(2\) each. He sells \(60\) pens at Rs. \(2.50\) each and remaining at Rs. \(1.50\) each. Find his profit/loss percentage.
A person bought a horse for Rs. \(1800\) and sold it for Rs. \(1755\). What is his loss percentage?
An article is marked \(40\%\) above its cost price and sold at a discount of \(15\%\). If the profit earned is Rs. \(176\), find the cost price.
A man sells two watches for Rs. \(990\) each. On one he loses \(10\%\) and on the other he gains \(10\%\). What is his overall gain or loss?
If selling price of \(8\) pencils is equal to cost price of \(10\) pencils, what is the profit percentage?
questions.keySolution:
SP of \(8\) pencils = CP of \(10\) pencils
Let CP per pencil = \(x\)
SP of \(8\) pencils = \(10x\)
SP per pencil = \(10x/8 = 1.25x\)
Profit \(\% = ((1.25x - x)/x) × 100 = 25\%\)

questions.stem: A trader allows a discount of \(15\%\) on marked price and still makes a profit of \(19\%\). What percentage above the cost price is the article marked?
questions.keySolution:
Let CP = \(100\)
SP for \(19\%\) profit = \(119\)
Let MP = \(x\)
After \(15\%\) discount: SP = \(0.85x = 119\)
Therefore, \(x = 119/0.85 = 140\)
Marked price is \(40\%\) above CP

questions.stem: By selling a chair for Rs. \(1050\), a carpenter loses \(16\%\). To gain \(20\%\), what should be the selling price?
A person buys goods for Rs. \(2400\) and wants to make \(25\%\) profit. If he gives \(8\%\) discount on marked price, what should be the marked price?

A merchant buys two items for Rs. \(600\). He sells one at \(22\%\) profit and other at \(12\%\) loss, but still gains Rs. \(6\) on the whole transaction. Find the cost price of the item sold at profit.
A shopkeeper fixes the price of an article in such a way that after giving discount of \(28\%\), he still gains \(8\%\). If the cost price is Rs. \(250\), what is the marked price?
The cost price of \(21\) articles is equal to selling price of \(18\) articles. Find the loss percentage.
questions.keySolution:
CP of \(21\) articles = SP of \(18\) articles
This means we're getting less money for more articles
Loss percentage = \((21-18)/21 × 100 = 3/21 × 100 = 14.29\%\)
